findings.retainedState: A prior listener's selected public track title,queue IDs and resume position remain visible/restored after logout to anonymous,login as another principal,reload,and direct account switch.
findings.rootCause: SessionQueryProvider correctly remounts all child component state on auth-scope occurrence; replacement PlayerProvider unconditionally loads unscoped persistent localStorage key tdf-global-player/v1. Session personal-data cleanup does not register or clear this key.
findings.playbackContinuity: Old native element is replaced and paused on logout; no automatic play restart observed. This is state carryover, not proved cross-account continuous audio.
findings.retention: Positions from both synthetic principals coexist in the same persistent positions map after queue replacement; no owner/expiry field in observed saved object.
findings.serverPrivateBytes: NOT_TESTED_OR_CLAIMED. Fixture tracks are explicitly synthetic public content; no actual delivery or backend authorization was exercised.

policyAssessment.explicit: ADR004 says queue,position and preferences persist; existing library docs isolate favorites,playlists,history by listener and analytics sessions rotate with identity.
policyAssessment.unresolved: No located explicit local queue persistence policy chooses device-wide shared public queue versus account-private listening state at logout/account switch.
policyAssessment.classification: Confirmed cross-principal client listening-state carryover; user-visible privacy/UX concern on shared browsers, not evidence of a server authorization bypass.
policyAssessment.possibleNextDecision: Separate harmless device preferences from listening state; root must choose desired anonymous-to-account and account-change retention policy before implementation.
